title: Unit, shift and scalar normalization of geometric point transport
statement: In the canonical point coordinates of [def-pod-point-weil-pairing-coordinates], with arbitrary D,l,E as there, geometric point Frobenius on the coefficient unit is the identity. For every rational point complex N, integer r and representative x:U→N[r], realizing c^{-1} P(x) followed by the pullback shift is the image of realize(x) under H^r(iota_N). Moreover every endomorphism h of U satisfies c^{-1} P(h) c=h. These claims use no tensor pairings and hold for all integer shifts and arbitrary rational arrows.

source.place: Final smooth-pairing clause; retained rational point-pairing argument, Steps 1--7.

proof.text:
The point transport [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] sends the constant section $1$ of the coefficient object to the section corresponding to $1$ under $c_s^{-1}$: restriction and the inverse-image coprojection keep $1$, and the comparison in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] sends it to $1\otimes1$, integrally to its compatible quotient family with zero cone coordinate. By [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] ($m=0$) and [def-weil-constant-weil-structure] (3), (4), $c_s=(c_R\lambda_R)\otimes1$ with $R_s=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$, and by [lem-pod-canonical-coefficient-pullback-reduction] (for $g=g_s$) this $\lambda_R$ is the canonical comparison with $\lambda_R\kappa_{R_s}=\mathrm{id}$; the existence-only $\lambda$ of the derived-pullback lemma alone would not fix this scalar. Hence $F(c_s)\iota_U=(\Gamma(s,c_R)\sigma_{R_s})\otimes E$, and the ring map $c_R$ sends the unit section $1$ of $g_s^{-1}R_s$ to $1$; rationalization preserves the equality. Thus $F(c_s)\iota_U=1_{FU}$. Naturality [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural], applied to $x:U\to A[i]$, now reads
$$\iota_{A[i]}F(x)=F(Px)\iota_U=F(Px\,c_s^{-1}).$$
With canonical shift comparisons understood, postcomposing with $F(\theta_{A[i]})$ gives the representative $\theta_{A[i]}P(x)c_s^{-1}$ of $F_Ax$. The same argument applies to $D$.

proof.text: Here are the shift identifications used in Step 2 and below. Restriction and the coprojection defining $\sigma$ act termwise, hence commute with $N[r]^j=N^{j+r}$ and its differential $(-1)^rd$. In the integral $\kappa$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], the mapping-fibre shift comparison is $(b,a)\mapsto((-1)^rb,a)$; it carries $(0,\theta(z))$ to $(0,\theta(z))$. Thus $\iota_{N[r]}=\iota_N[r]$ under the pullback shift comparison; this persists after rationalization [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For tensor shifts use the total-model formula $t_{u,v}(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{vp}x\otimes y$ on first shifted degree $p$ [lem-pur-total-tensor-signed-coherence]. Pullback preserves degrees and scalars, so its tensor comparison has this same coefficient on both routes of the shift square. At the completed stage this is a levelwise identity on the reduction tower; the product and cone shift comparison is exactly the one specified in [lem-sf-completed-tensor-shift-right]. Consequently it is also an identity for the completed comparisons and their rational images. This checks both zero and successive shifts, for all integers, without permuting the factors.

proof.text:
By Step 1 write $h=\lambda1_U$ for its unique scalar $\lambda\in E$. The rational pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is $E$-linear: its defining formula is $P(u\otimes\lambda)=P(u)\otimes\lambda$. Hence
$$cP(h)c^{-1}=c(\lambda1_{PU})c^{-1}=\lambda1_U=h.$$
Combining with Step 5 proves both displayed equations. The construction uses morphisms in the derived category and its functorial tensor, so it is independent of any chain representatives. All shifts and their inverses were allowed in Step 3. For a zero object the corresponding Hom group is zero and both expressions vanish. The calculation uses only rational arrows and their stated Weil equations, so an integral model for $\theta_A$ or $\theta_D$, and in particular a stable integral lattice, has not been imposed.

lean.statement: theorem point_weil_transport_unit_shift : frobenius D l hl E (U D l hl E) (c D l hl E) = 𝟙 _ ∧ (∀ (N : C D l E) (r : ℤ) (x : U D l hl E ⟶ N⟦r⟧), realize D l hl E ((P D l hl E).obj N) r (transportRep D l hl E N r x) = (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{u} (ModuleCat.{u} E) r).map (iota D l hl E N) (realize D l hl E N r x)) ∧ (∀ h : U D l hl E ⟶ U D l hl E, (c D l hl E).inv ≫ (P D l hl E).map h ≫ (c D l hl E).hom = h)
